text: foundry-toolchain is the official GitHub Action that installs Foundry on a runner. A real workflow checks out the repo, installs Foundry, formats, builds, and tests — on every push and pull request.

submodules recursive matters specifically here, since Foundry dependencies are usually git submodules. forge fmt check fails the build without rewriting; forge build sizes catches the 24 kilobyte deploy limit early.
Every push and PR triggers a run, visible in the repo's Actions tab as a list — status, branch, and duration at a glance.
Clicking into a run shows the job summary — trigger, status, and total duration.
And the step-by-step log, where a failed forge test step shows you the actual revert or assertion failure.
This is the pre-deploy gate from Lesson 7, actually running. Lesson 9 adds the next layer — automated linting and static analysis, in the same pipeline.
